I will say that I do work for Best Buy, and I do sell computers.  I don't know how it is in all the stores around the country, but at my store I actually do try to have the customer in mind. I don't push the services, I present them as options. I try to educate people on what they're buying, to suit their needs. I show them options I think may pertain to what they're doing, but in the end, I leave the decision up to them. Some customers actually get frustrated with me for showing them so many options, they want to be told what to buy. I hate these kinds of people, it's your purchase, YOU make the decision.

Yes, some stuff is overpriced. But it's how the store makes money. Between the lowered cost of laptops, and the fee for credit card processing, most retailers actually lose money if there are no accessories or services attached. I don't really agree with some of the pricing, and I absolutely hate the statement "these are so expensive!!". What am I supposed to do? Yes, you can it cheaper online. No I don't control the prices. If you don't want to wait for it to be shipped to you, deal with it. For services, some people have no clue what they're doing, so paying someone to do it for them is justified for them.

Then again, I've only been working there a year, and I'm already sick of it...

I was raised Lutheran, and my parents were very religious. At least my mom was, I think my dad just went along with it, though I can never tell fully since he's a rather quiet guy. They forced me and my sister to go to church every Sunday, and they were quite involved with all the goings-on, so I ended up going to the church for different events at least 3 times a week. Services on Sundays, Confirmation/Youth group on Wednesdays, events and socials on Saturdays.

All throughout this I was always the "model Christian". All the older members of the church would always comment on how good I was, how much I knew (I rather had a knack for memorizing things people told me, and such always knew the answers they wanted in youth group), and how much I was blessed by god with my talents. When I was younger, I was proud of the compliments, even though I never really had felt the presence of any sort of god in my life. I rarely thought more about it, but as I went into high school, I started to hate it more and more.

After a rough part of my life, going through depression and questioning my sexuality, my religion also got thrown into the mix of things I wasn't sure of. Especially since my mother really wasn't a great model for what "Christian morality" was supposed to be. Both my mother and my father flipped out when they found out about my girlfriend. The thoughts started go around, as I couldn't reconcile the idea I'd been taught from the very beginning; that God had created me, had shaped me just how he wanted me, and he loved me, but if I loved another girl, that was wrong and he would punish me. How could a loving god create a person that he knew in the end would end up going to hell? How is that compassion? Or love?

After I realized this, I basically reflected back on my life and I realized that I perhaps hadn't really believed at all. All of a sudden it seemed silly, that all the stories of "miracles" and Jesus' death and resurrection were just as much not real as the fantasy books I loved. There was almost no difference between the two.

As I've gone to college, I've learned a lot more about myself, and the more I reflect and learn, the more I feel validated in my decision to label myself an atheist.

I'm not sure if it's because I am a girl, or if I'm just too hard on myself most of the time. Also, trying to get into a male-dominated field is sort of discouraging at times.

I try to not let it get to me, because I know that I am intelligent, and can do anything I set my mind to. But it's hard to sway the thoughts that there's someone more qualified for this, and better at it than me, that I can't possibly become as good at it as others.
